borough: London Borough of Barking and Dagenham
decision_conditions:
The scale, siting and design of the proposed development would result in an increased sense of overbearingness and a harmful loss of outlook and daylight to neighbouring occupiers, therefore constituting unneighbourly development and contrary to:

  • National Planning Policy Framework  (NPPF) (December, 2024)
  • Policy D6 of the London Plan (March 2021)  
  • The Residential Extensions and Alterations Supplementary Planning Document (February 2012);
  • Policies SP2, DMD1 and DMD5 of The Barking and Dagenham Local Plan (September, 2024)

The proposed development, by reason of siting, scale, mass and design, would be an excessively bulky, discordant addition which would would appear overly dominant and not have regard to the original built form of the host dwelling and the area. The proposal would introduce a massing which would be insubordinate to the dwelling and result in an abnormally large dwelling. Its design does not reflect the character of the area, and does not have regard to the key characteristics which make up the street scene. The proposal is therefore found to be at odds with the following policies which seek to ensure that development proposals have regard to the existing character:

  • National Planning Policy Framework (NPPF) (December, 2024)
  • Policy D4 of the London Plan (March 2021)
  • The Residential Extensions and Alterations Supplementary Planning Document (February 2012)
  • Policies SP2, DMD1 and DMD5 of The Barking and Dagenham Local Plan (September, 2024)
description: Construction of a two storey side and rear extension and the construction of a rear and side dormer extension including two roof lights to the front to facilitate conversion of roof space into habitable accommodation
